Good catch on the instinct — but actually, a min heap is the right move here, even though it feels backwards. Let me show you why it works. Let's walk through a real example. Say we want the 2nd largest in [3, 1, 4, 2]. I'll push numbers in and keep only k of them. We start the loop. Push 3 in — heap is [3], size is 1, which is not bigger than k, so we keep it. Push 1 — heap is [1, 3], size is 2, still not bigger than k. Push 4 — now the heap is [1, 3, 4], size is 3, which is bigger than 2, so we pop the smallest one, which is 1.
